formal_title: Non-Nested Architecture Rival Construction, Minimal Separating Intervention Basis, Opposed Counterfactual Prediction Design, Interventional Kernel Rank, Architecture Equivalence-Class Refinement, Quotient/Gate Cross-Coupling Stress, Latent-Transport Obstruction Search & Macro-Architecture Identifiability Court
scientific_target: Replace nested U0⊂U1 comparison with non-nested architectures that make opposed predictions under a minimal frozen intervention basis, then identify only the interventional equivalence class justified by the measured kernel.

observables.default_decision: y=q∧g unless a rival explicitly predicts otherwise

N0_LAYER_INDEPENDENT_MEDIATION.structure: upstream transport feeds q; local control independently sets g; y=q∧g

N1_CROSS_COUPLED_CONTROL.structure: the admitted upstream transport state also controls/reconfigures the local gate; q and g are not layer-independent

non_nestedness.statement: N0 and N1 are non-nested under the frozen intervention typing because upstream DROP/RESTORE require contradictory gate effects: N0 requires Δg=0, N1 requires Δg=Δq on the separating states.

minimal_separating_basis.theorem_target: One upstream DROP intervention with direct measurement of q and g separates N0 and N1 if it is validly typed and starts at q=g=1; local-gate DROP is a negative control, not a separator.
minimal_separating_basis.redundancy_test: Determine whether RESTORE adds rank/information after DROP under the measured kernel.

interventional_kernel.rank_field: rational numbers over observed signed effects; GF(2) rank reported only as a parity diagnostic, not primary authority
interventional_kernel.rank_target: rank of the frozen intervention-response matrix across admitted interventions
interpretation: rank 1: one effective latent direction under the frozen observables
rank 2: quotient and gate perturbations expose two independent observable directions
rank 3: action contains an additional intervention direction not mediated by measured q/g, challenging the two-layer factorization

quotient_gate_cross_coupling.obstruction_definition: A typed upstream-only intervention changes g after q/g normalization is frozen.
quotient_gate_cross_coupling.adjudication: Measured Δg on the frozen separator chooses between N0 and N1 unless intervention typing itself fails prospectively.

search_for: action change at Δq=0 and Δg=0
same normalized q,g with different y under matched environment
mechanism-specific hidden variable required to explain separator
noncommuting upstream interventions whose effect cannot be represented by the frozen q quotient
latent_transport_obstruction.consequence: Any such exact witness blocks both N0 and N1 and reopens the latent-state/quotient design.

decomposition_equivalence.identified_object: equivalence class of architectures inducing the same frozen interventional kernel K_I
decomposition_equivalence.uniqueness_rule: claim a unique rival only if N0 and N1 yield distinct kernels on the admitted basis and the measured kernel matches exactly one
decomposition_equivalence.no_claim_if: intervention typing is ambiguous, q/g cannot be measured independently, or both rivals induce the same measured kernel

empirical_strategy.lane_A: Find fresh mechanism with an upstream state change known to independently preserve local gate; expected N0 witness.
empirical_strategy.lane_B: Find fresh mechanism where upstream negotiation/detection explicitly toggles local enablement gate; expected N1 witness.
empirical_strategy.strong_court: At least one exact mechanism for each non-nested rival, plus a shared measurement protocol, so the rival class is not defined from one mechanism after outcome.

mathematical_targets: prove non-nestedness from contradictory Δg constraints
prove one-intervention separator minimality under direct q/g observation
derive kernel-rank interpretation and its limits
show rank 3 falsifies complete mediation by q,g under deterministic y
characterize equivalence under a finite intervention basis
